newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE LOCAL SHARES CLOSE OFF HIGHS.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE LOCAL SHARES CLOSE OFF HIGHS.

text.p: Local tranches of Singapore blue chips ended firmer though off their highs on Thursday in choppy trading.
Dealers said foreign tranches of blue chips also bounced off their lows but still ended in negative territory on concerns that foreign shareholding limits may be removed eventually.

"There was talk of the authorities coming out with a statement on the foreign shares, so traders were generally less aggressive in the afternoon in chasing local and dumping foreign shares," a dealer with a Singapore brokerage said.
The Stock Exchange of Singapore and the Monetary Authority of Singapore did not issue any statements during the trading day.

DBS Bank was among the top gainers, closing 60 cents up at S$9.40 after touching a 1997 high of S$9.65. Volume was an active 944,000 shares. Its foreign tranche bounced off an intraday low of S$17.50 to end at S$18.10, down 70 cents.
Singapore Airlines also surged to a year high of S$8.00 before easing back to S$7.75, down 30 cents. The foreign shares shed 50 cents to end at S$12.50.
